assessment.majorBlockers: The backend dev server silently died mid-session (no graceful-shutdown log, no crash dump), destroying the live session; recovery auto-restarted the server but left a two-tabs-same-URL state in which commands reported success without affecting the page being read, and freshly taken refs were rejected as stale — resolved only by close + fresh open.

issues.title: `get attr`/`get property` reports 'No elements matched' when the element exists but the value is empty

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s form-fill-eval get attr "#first-name" data-bogus-xyz    (visible, filled field; attribute genuinely absent)
Expected per the documented value contract: `""` = element matched, value absent.
Also: ./b4w.ps1 -s form-fill-eval get property "#phone-number" value  (existing input, empty value)
And for structured proof: append --json → {"status":"ok",...,"output":{"result":"","selector":"#first-name"}} (note: no "mode" field).

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: A matched element with an absent/empty attribute or property should print the value ("") plus the matched-but-empty diagnostic the CLI claims to emit for attr/property modes ("Element matched but the attribute 'data-bogus-xyz' is empty or missing — or no element matched"), consistent with SKILL.md §5's value contract ("" = matched, empty; null = no match).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Prints an empty line followed by the generic branch: "No elements matched \"#first-name\"." / "The `get` command resolves refs against the live page; CSS selector support varies by mode and backend resolution." / htmlsnapshot advice. This falsely says the selector matched nothing and suggests picking different selectors — it misled the evaluation into concluding a hidden input could not be resolved when it resolved fine. `--json` output confirms the element matched (result "") and shows no "mode" field.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The `get` command's tool_params_fn in commands.rs builds params as {selector, propName} or {selector, attrName} and never includes a `mode` (or `name`) key — the mode is encoded only in the MCP tool name (select_first_property_value_or_null / select_first_attribute_or_null). handle_get() in main.rs reads tool_params["mode"], gets None, defaults to "text", so get_no_value_diagnostic_lines() (main.rs:8394) takes the generic else branch instead of the mode-aware attr/property branch at line 8405. The existing unit test get_attr_null_message_does_not_claim_no_elements_matched (main.rs:30401) calls the helper directly with mode="attr" and therefore passes while the production wiring never passes that mode. Additionally the empty_result check treats "" (matched-but-empty) and "null" (no match) identically, so even a correct message would be attached to the wrong case.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/commands.rs:1636 (get tool_params_fn); cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:8428 (handle_get), 8394 (get_no_value_diagnostic_lines)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Propagate the mode (and the attr/property name) into tool_params in commands.rs, e.g. add "mode": "property"/"attr" and "name": name to the emitted JSON, so handle_get's diagnostics select the intended branch.
- Branch on the actual result: keep "No elements matched" only for JSON null; for the empty-string case print the matched-but-empty wording (and never suggest changing selectors).
- Add an end-to-end test that runs the real command path (tool_params_fn -> handle_get formatting), not just the diagnostic helper, so the wiring gap cannot regress.
- Optionally render an explicit marker for the empty case (e.g. `(empty)`) so humans can tell "matched, empty" from "no match" at a glance.

issues.title: Backend silently died mid-session; the CLI misreported it as 'No active browser session' and the live session was lost

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
In dev mode, run a normal multi-step flow (open → snapshot → fill → click → snapshot -v 0). Mid-session (backend log shows activity until 00:04:06) the backend at 127.0.0.1:8285 stopped responding. Next command: ./b4w.ps1 -s form-fill-eval fill e8 "Acme Corp" →
  Error: No active browser session. Run 'browser4-cli.exe open <url>' or 'browser4-cli.exe goto <url>' first to load a page, then try 'fill' again.  (exit 3)
Only ./b4w.ps1 list revealed: "Browser4 backend is not started or unreachable at http://127.0.0.1:8285." with the session listed as Status Unknown / Next open Refresh.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: A distinct, honest error when the backend port is closed (naming host:port and the actual cause), plus either transparent auto-restart of the backend for page-dependent commands or accurate guidance that the backend went down and the live session/page state will be lost.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The command blamed the session ('No active browser session') even though the session existed — it was the server that was gone. For this command class no auto-restart was attempted; a later command (page-info) silently restarted the server (13.2s) and then reported 'Session refresh needed' — the live browser state (my submitted form page) was unrecoverable. The backend's own log shows entries up to 00:04:06 and then the next instance's startup at 00:05:35 with no graceful-shutdown lines; no hs_err_pid file exists; the log segment covering the death window was not retained in the bundle logs (rotation), so the trigger is unlogged.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Two layers. (1) CLI: the pre-dispatch gate at main.rs:27380-27391 returns the hard-coded 'No active browser session' CliError (ExitCode::Session) whenever the local backend port is closed for a page-dependent command, conflating 'backend unreachable' with 'no session' — and it returns before ensure_server_running() can restart the server. (2) Backend: the JVM stopped without logging any shutdown sequence and without a crash dump, which points to abrupt external termination (e.g. a kill from another process active in the same checkout/workspace — evidence of heavy concurrent activity: the same runtime bundle logged six backend startups between 21:18 and 23:53, agent-trace logs exist for tasks at 23:40-23:54 in this workspace, and another Browser4 instance holds port 8088). Exact cause needs investigation (audit process kills; preserve the previous instance's log across restarts).

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:27380 (should_ensure_server_running gate; error constructed at 27387); backend lifecycle/logging in cli/browser4-cli/src/daemon.rs

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Replace the message with a backend-aware error: state that the Browser4 server at <host:port> is not running/unreachable, that the live browser session state will be lost if it is restarted, and which command will restart it.
- For page-dependent commands with a saved session, attempt the same auto-start path other commands use (or explicitly document why it is skipped) instead of failing outright.
- Preserve the previous backend instance's log across restarts (unique rotated names) so a crash window is always diagnosable; log a beacon on unexpected JVM termination (shutdown hook / launcher wrapper).
- Document in the dev-mode/session docs that a backend restart invalidates live sessions (browser survives; tabs/state do not) and how to recover deterministically.

issues.title: Post-crash recovery left a duplicate-tab session where commands reported success without effect and fresh refs failed as 'stale'

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
After the crash in Issue 2, let the next command auto-restart the backend, then interact with the recovered session:
  ./b4w.ps1 -s form-fill-eval fill e3 "Ada"  → [INTERNAL] browser_type failed: fill: no element found for selector [backend:3]. The selector may be stale — re-run `snapshot` to refresh refs.
  ./b4w.ps1 -s form-fill-eval click e12        → ✓ Clicked e12   (but contact method stayed 'email' in the page state)
  ./b4w.ps1 -s form-fill-eval fill e7 "+1 555 013 4237" → ✓ Filled  (but phoneNumber stayed "")
  ./b4w.ps1 -s form-fill-eval tab-list         → TWO tabs with the identical URL, no active-tab marker
  ./b4w.ps1 -s form-fill-eval eval "window.__browser4State..." (after tab-select 1) → NO_STATE
The same refs (e3, e12, e7) worked immediately in a fresh close+open session.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: A recovered session has one deterministic active tab; a `✓` confirmation means the action affected the page the user reads back; refs from the most recent snapshot resolve as long as the document is unchanged.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The reconnected browser contained two tabs of the same URL; different commands resolved/interacted with different tabs (or read state from a tab the actions never touched), producing (a) stale-ref 'no element found [backend:3]' errors seconds after a snapshot with no navigation, and (b) false success confirmations for click/fill that changed nothing on the observed page. The phone fill 'succeeded' into a still-hidden field and was discarded by the page, compounding the confusion.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: After a backend restart the session manager re-attaches to the still-running browser but does not normalize its tab state: a pre-existing/leftover tab of the same URL survives alongside the re-opened one, and the session's active-tab pointer is unset (tab-list showed no active marker until an explicit tab-select). The CLI has no cross-check that the tab it mutates is the tab it snapshots/reads. The exact per-command tab resolution needs investigation in PulsarSessionManager.getOrRecoverSession and the CLI's session/tab targeting.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: browser4-rest session recovery (PulsarSessionManager.getOrRecoverSession); CLI tab targeting (cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs, with_session / tab handling)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- On recovery, deterministically select an active tab and either close duplicate tabs of the same URL or explicitly report 'N tabs found; using tab <n>'.
- Always render the active-tab marker in `tab-list` (currently it only appears after an explicit `tab-select`), so users can see which tab commands will hit.
- Before mutating, validate the resolved target against the tab snapshot was taken from; fail loudly instead of reporting ✓ when the ref resolves in a different document/tab.
- Detect 'document replaced since snapshot' per tab so refs fail with an accurate reason rather than 'stale selector' after a restart.

issues.title: Hidden conditional fields are unmarked in snapshots, `fill` reports success when the page discards the value, and the form-fill recipe omits `--verify`

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
On the same fixture (contact method = Email):
  ./b4w.ps1 -s form-fill-eval snapshot -i  → lists 'textbox "tel phone-number phoneNumber +1 555 123 4567" [ref=e7]' with no hidden marker (only the missing [box=...] hints)
  ./b4w.ps1 -s form-fill-eval fill e7 "+1 555 123 4567" → ✓ Filled
  ./b4w.ps1 -s form-fill-eval get text "#result-data" after submit → "phoneNumber": ""  (the page's updateDynamicFields() clears values of non-active conditional fields)
Using the documented-only-in-help flag: ./b4w.ps1 -s form-fill-eval fill e7 "..." --verify would have reported the read-back mismatch.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Interactive elements that are not rendered (display:none / zero box) should be distinguishable in snapshot output (e.g. a [hidden] annotation), and the canonical form-fill workflow (SKILL.md copy-paste template / quick-patterns.md §2) should show `fill --verify` so silent value loss is caught at interaction time.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The `-i` snapshot presents hidden conditional fields like ordinary textboxes; `fill` prints a plain `✓ Filled` although the page immediately discards the value; the loss surfaces only later in the submitted payload. The `--verify` flag exists (shown in `help fill`) but is absent from every form-filling recipe.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The snapshot renderer emits [box=...] only for rendered elements and adds no annotation for the hidden case, so hiddenness is only inferable from a missing box on interactive nodes. The skill/quick-pattern form-fill recipes document --submit but not --verify, unlike `type`/`select` whose recipes mention verification.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs (snapshot rendering / box emission); skills/browser4-cli/references/quick-patterns.md (Interactive Form Fill, §2); skills/browser4-cli/SKILL.md (copy-paste template)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Annotate interactive elements without a layout box in snapshot/-i output (e.g. `[hidden]` or `[box=0x0]`), so agents and users can tell a conditional/invisible field before filling it.
- Add `--verify` to the canonical form-fill example in SKILL.md and quick-patterns.md, and mention that a conditional field filled while hidden can be cleared by page JS.
- When --verify detects a mismatch, add a hint that the element may be hidden/conditional or that page script may have cleared it, instead of only reporting the raw mismatch.

issues.title: `select` prints an unlabeled raw JSON array before the friendly confirmation

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 -s form-fill-eval select e6 "Singapore"
Output:
  ["sg"]
  ✓ Selected 'Singapore' in e6

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Human-readable mode prints one clear confirmation line (optionally including the resolved value); the raw payload appears only under --json or is clearly labeled.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: A bare JSON array `["sg"]` is printed with no context before the confirmation — it reads like debug output and a first-time user cannot tell what it means (it is the selected option's value).

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The select handler prints the raw non-empty tool response verbatim in human mode (main.rs:12772-12775 — if !text.is_empty() { cli_println!("{}", text); }) before emitting the '✓ Selected…' line; for select the raw response is the JSON array of selected values.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs:12772 (select handler raw echo)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Suppress the raw echo in human mode when it is just the selected-values array, or format it (e.g. `Selected values: sg`).
- Fold the resolved value into the confirmation: `✓ Selected 'Singapore' (value: sg)` — keeps the useful label→value mapping without the stray line.
- Keep the raw array only in --json output.
